title: First Responder Protocols, Availability Matrix, and Communication Templates
author: Ava Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the first-responder responsibilities, an availability matrix for responder coverage, escalation heuristics, and ready-to-use communication templates for customer-facing status updates and internal bridge notes. It is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, support, and incident commanders.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood Inference production services (examples: redwood-api, redwood-serving, control-plane, kv-cache, routing-proxy). Does not replace existing service-specific runbooks; it complements them with standard response patterns and message templates.

1) Responder availability matrix (how to interpret coverage)

Columns: Role | Primary responsibility | Typical page window | Expected ack | Typical handoff
- Primary on-call: Service triage, mitigation, short-term remediation | 24x7 | 5 minutes | Handoff to secondary or platform after 2 hours
- Secondary on-call: Tier-2 escalation, deep-dive assistance, cross-service coordination | business hours + weekends followups | 30 minutes | Take ownership if primary unavailable for >30m
- Platform SRE: Capacity/fleet & region failover | business hours with on-call rotation | 60 minutes | Coordinate region failover actions
- Incident Commander (IC): Incident lifecycle & stakeholder comms | invoked as needed | 15 minutes | Own incident timeline until postmortem

Availability rules (operationalized):
- Pager windows and contactable status must be reflected in the oncall roster and Slack presence flags.
- If a primary on-call does not ack within expected ack time, the pager policy escalates to secondary, then to IC escalation roster.

2) Severity definitions and primary actions (quick reference)

- Sev0 (Critical outage; customer-impacting, no viable fallback):
  - Target ack: 2 minutes.
  - Actions: Immediate bridge (Zoom/Jabber), route traffic to fallback region/model variant if possible, engage IC, notify GTM/CS for customer-impact comms.
  - Escalation window: 5 minutes to engage leadership.

- Sev1 (Major degradation; significant error rate or latency regression affecting many customers):
  - Target ack: 5 minutes.
  - Actions: Open bridge, start triage (service logs, SLO dashboards, recent deploys), enable circuit-breakers or rate-limits, begin customer status draft.

- Sev2 (Partial degradation; single region or small customer subset impacted):
  - Target ack: 15 minutes.
  - Actions: Triage with limited bridge, consider failover, prepare targeted customer comms if impact persists >1 hour.

- Sev3 (Non-urgent; operational issue with no immediate customer impact):
  - Target ack: 4 hours.
  - Actions: Create a ticket, assign owner, schedule remediation in next sprint.

3) Escalation heuristics (decision ladder)

1. Detect & verify: Confirm alert validity (noise reduction) using dashboard checks and log sampling.
2. Contain & stabilize: If possible, apply safe mitigations (temporary scaling, circuit-breakers, config rollback).
3. Communicate & coordinate: Stand up bridge for Sev1/Sev0. Assign IC for coordination.
4. Restore & validate: Restore to SLOs. Validate using synthetic traffic and customer probes.
5. Post-incident actions: Create postmortem within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev0. Track action items to completion.

Decision heuristics guidance: When in doubt between rollback vs patch, prefer the action that minimizes customer impact and risk to data integrity. Prefer rolling back to a known-good model/service image if confidence in a forward fix is <75% and customers are impacted.

4) Standard operating checklists (for primary on-call)

Immediate triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Record incident start time and initial signals.
2) Confirm which services and regions are affected.
3) Identify recent deploys or config changes in the last 60 minutes.
4) Enable temporary throttles or scale-up GPU pools for the affected service if safe.
5) Notify secondary and platform SRE.
6) Prepare initial external status message (template below).

Containment checklist (15–60 minutes):
- If the source is a noisy neighbor (noisy model or heavy prefix usage), apply request-shed rules or route to degraded model variant.
- If KV cache corruption suspected, divert read-only requests and start cache rebuild in background.
- If control-plane errors: evaluate KMS/HSM calls and audit logs before mass restarts.

Restore checklist (60–180 minutes):
- Run validated smoke tests and synthetic requests.
- Confirm token-level cost anomaly is resolved (if the cause was runaway generation).
- Gradually re-enable traffic and monitor 1-minute SLO windows.

5) Game day & drills (how to run targeted exercises)

Purpose: Validate the response cadence and train responders on specific failure modes (KV-cache thrash, multi-region failover, inference kernel regression).

Game day structure (3 hours typical):
- 0:00–0:20: Briefing & objectives (owner, SLOs under test, allowed mitigations).
- 0:20–1:00: Inject failures (synthetic latency, CPU/GPU saturation, KV eviction).
- 1:00–2:00: Live response & triage, using real oncall tooling and customer comms.
- 2:00–2:40: Focused postmortem (blameless) and action item identification.
- 2:40–3:00: Retrospective & roll-forward tasks (document updates).

Scoring rubric (sample):
- Time-to-first-ack (target <5m), bridge establishment (<10m for Sev1), and customer message publish (<30m).
- SLO re-entry time and correctness of rollback decisions counted in scoring.

6) Communication templates

A) Initial internal bridge note (copy into bridge chat).
"Incident detected: [service] - [short description]. Severity: [Sev]. Time: [HH:MM UTC]. Affects: [regions/customers]. Initial actions: triaging, scaling, bridge underway. Primary: @oncall-primary, Secondary: @oncall-secondary. IC: [name]. URL: [dashboard link]"

B) Initial customer-facing status (status.redwood.ai style short message)
"Status: Investigating - [Short headline]
Current impact: Customers in [region/segment] may experience [latency/errors].
What we’re doing: Our engineers have identified the affected subsystem and are implementing mitigations.
Next update: We will provide an update by [time + 30m].
Internal reference: INC-[YYYYMMDD]-[NNN]"

C) Customer update (30–60 minutes)
"Status: Mitigating - [headline]
Summary: We have applied [rollback/fallback/model-variant-route] which reduced error rate from X% to Y%.
Work underway: Continuing root cause analysis and validation. Estimated resolution: [ETA or TBD].
Contacts: support@redwood.ai for case-specific questions."

D) Resolution message (final)
"Status: Resolved - [headline]
Summary: Root cause: [brief root cause statement]. What we did: [actions taken]. Customer impact: [duration, percent affected]. Postmortem: A post-incident report will be published at [link] and action items will be tracked.
Thank you for your patience."

E) Internal severity escalation alert (Slack snippet)
"SEV[0/1] ALERT: [service] | Impact: [short]. IC: [name]. Bridge: [link]. Immediate asks: (1) Stop new deploys to [service]. (2) Run smoke test ID [id]. (3) Confirm rollback permission."

7) Post-incident requirements

- For Sev0/Sev1: Postmortem draft due within 72 hours. Postmortem must include timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation timeline, and prioritized action items with owners and due dates.
- For Sev2: Blameless incident note and follow-up ticket within 7 days.
- Evidence to collect: relevant logs (retention: 90 days standard), SLO graphs (1m/5m windows), deploy hashes, configuration diffs, and customer reports.

Template for postmortem headers (copy into the postmortem doc):
- Title: [Service] incident [date] - [short headline]
- Severity: [Sev]
- Start/End: [timestamps]
- Impact summary: [customers, regions, features]
- Timeline (annotated)
- Root cause analysis
- Immediate mitigations performed
- Long-term remediation and owners
- Follow-up verification plan

8) Roster hygiene & handoffs

- On-call engineers must keep calendars updated and mark out-of-office on the schedule.
- Handoffs: send a 10–15 minute handoff message in the rota channel summarizing active incidents, outstanding action items, and any ongoing mitigations.
- If a handoff occurs during a Sev1/Sev0, the outgoing primary must do a synchronous voice handoff.

9) Tools and dashboards referenced (examples)

- SLO dashboard: /dashboards/slo-global (1m/5m windows)
- Alerting: Pager system (rules link), Slack alert channel #ops-alerts
- Bridge: zoom.us/redwood-ops or internal bridge tool
- Incident tracking: INC-[YYYYMMDD]-NNN ticketing system

10) Ownership & review cadence

- Document owner: eng-sre (primary).
- Quarterly review: Required for coverage rules, escalation windows, and templates. Update after each major incident where communication cadence failed expectations.

Appendix A — Quick reference: sample commands and checks

- Check recent deploys:
  curl -s https://deploys.redwood.internal/api/recent?service=redwood-serving | jq .
- Restart canary router (safe pattern):
  kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/router-canary --grace-period=60
- Pull recent SLO window:
  ./slo-cli query --service redwood-api --window 1m --metric p99_latency

Appendix B — Example status page timeline (for customer transparency)

- T+0: Investigating (initial message)
- T+30: Mitigating (first update, what changed)
- T+60: We have reduced impact by [X%] (update)
- T+120: Restoration in progress; ETA if known
- T+resolved: Resolved (final & postmortem link)

Appendix C — Glossary

- IC: Incident Commander
- KV-cache: Key/value inference cache used by serving runtime
- Noisy neighbor: A model or request stream consuming disproportionate resources

Document maintenance: This page should be updated after each game day and after any incident where communication cadence, templates, or escalation windows were insufficient.

Last reviewed by: Marcus Lee (eng-sre) on 2027-02-28
